title: Integrated hand truck with sized brake linkage
problem_restatement: Lift and lower 60 kg load step by step on stairs with one operator, hold without grip, fold flat under 15 kg for van stowage.
mechanism_sentence: Two three-wheeled side clusters roll over each stair nose while a hand crank through a self-locking screw gear lifts a 60 kg parcel one 170 mm step at a time with about 98 N of hand effort and holds it parked when you let go.
decisive_choices: Use tri-star clusters with 150 mm wheels for 170 mm risers
Use 15 to 1 self-locking worm plus pawl with 0.25 m crank for 98.1 N effort and hands-free hold
Use twin-tube aluminium spine with 2-step fold to 1200x600x300 mm under 15 kg
open_question: What is pawl tooth shear stress and wear life under 6.13 kN repeated parking load?
transfer_line: Load: closed-loop handle -> self-locking worm drive -> tri-star cluster | Measured: hand pull -> cluster torque

assumed_constraints.constraint: design stairs riser 170 mm tread 280 mm stair angle about 31 deg based on residential range 150-190 mm riser 250-300 mm tread
two-hand closed-loop handle height 900-1100 mm adjustable, grip diameter 30 mm, sustained pull under 150 N per operator based on Snook psychophysical limits
frame carries 60 kg load plus 15 kg device with safety factor 2 on yield and folded envelope 1200x600x300 mm for van aisle and door stowage

functional_decomposition: Lift and lower 60 kg load step by step on stairs with one operator
Hold load on stair slope without continuous operator grip force
Operate up and down stairs with two-hand posture and effort one courier can sustain
Carry 60 kg load with frame weight under 15 kg and fold flat for van stowage
Secure 60 kg parcels up to 800 mm and stow folded device in van with 5-minute field service

concept.working_principle: Tri-star clusters rotate 120 deg per step to lift load one riser, worm plus pawl locks axle hands-free, hand crank through 15 to 1 reduction drives climb and dead-man lever holds descent, twin-tube frame carries load and folds flat.

parts.name: L-frame spine twin tubes
parts.function: carry 60 kg load with frame weight under 15 kg

parts.name: telescopic closed-loop handle with dead-man brake lever

key_estimates.quantity: energy to lift 60 kg one riser
handle pull from cluster torque and 1.2 m lever
hand pull with 15 to 1 worm and 0.25 m crank
pawl tooth force from cluster torque
dead-man lever force from worm shaft torque
twin-tube modulus margin vs SF2 requirement
total device mass from parts breakdown
pin double shear stress for fold lock
lift energy 15 kg device into van floor 0.6 m
reduction ratio to bring handle pull below target

fabrication_steps.description: Cut and assemble twin-tube spine with steel hinge inserts
Fit hinged toe plate and telescopic closed-loop handle with brake lever
Mount tri-star clusters with solid wheels on worm axle with pawl and crank
Fit straps, skid pads and quick pins and check flat fold

risks.risk: handle effort overrun on tri-star cluster
risks.mitigation: use 15 to 1 worm with 0.25 m crank to give 98.1 N below 150 N limit

risks.risk: thin 1.18 margin and pin collapse on stairs
risks.mitigation: use two tubes giving 2.88 cm3 against 2.45 cm3 required with steel pins

risks.risk: descent runaway if brake linkage fails
risks.mitigation: hold with self-locking worm plus pawl and 61.3 N dead-man squeeze with uphill stance

novelty_claim: Integrated hand truck with tri-star cluster, self-locking worm plus pawl crank and 2-step flat fold

figure_spec.system_view: Side view of tri-star cluster on two stair noses, 150 mm wheels, crank and worm brake on axle

open_questions: What is pawl tooth shear stress and wear life under 6.13 kN repeated parking load?
Does 5 s per stair and 60 s per flight remain acceptable across full courier rounds?
